title: DR1 stops a user who says the consignment has a region of origin code but leaves the code blank; the frontend lets them continue with nothing entered.

finding.frontend: The origin page's only rule about the region code is a maximum length. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-86 composes a required rule for the country, an allowed-values rule for the Yes/No answer and maxText rules for the code and the internal reference, and there is no rule tying the code to the Yes answer. The feature's copy file carries errors for a missing country and for an over-long code but none for a missing code, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/copy/copy.en.js:21-28. Choosing Yes and pressing Save and continue with the revealed field empty therefore saves and moves on.
finding.prototype: Choosing Yes and leaving the code blank is rejected: DR1 raises "Enter the region of origin code" against the revealed field and lists it in the "There is a problem" summary, linked to the input. It is the only rule DR1 enforces on this page.
finding.difference: Add a rule that requires the region of origin code when the region-of-origin question is answered Yes, with the message "Enter the region of origin code", and leave it out of scope when the answer is No. One validator and one copy string. Sequence it with the prefix change to the same field so the required rule lands on whichever control ends up collecting the code.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting the frontend's origin page with the region question answered Yes and the code empty and being stopped on that page — no error state for this page was captured on either side, so the claim rests on the composed rule list in the origin controller, which has no required rule for regionOfOriginCode.
finding.verification: Read the composed rule list at origin/controller.js:63-86: requiredOneOf on countryOfOrigin, oneOf on regionOfOriginCodeRequirement, maxText on regionOfOriginCode and internalReferenceNumber, and a pattern rule on internalReferenceNumber. There is no required rule for regionOfOriginCode, and copy.en.js:21-28 carries countryRequired, regionCodeMaxLength, internalReferenceMaxLength and internalReferencePattern and nothing for a missing code. Both citations resolve exactly. On the DR1 side, app/routes.js:246-263 is validateOriginOfImport and its single branch is `regionOfOriginRequired === 'Yes' && !regionOfOriginCodeSuffix`, pushing "Enter the region of origin code" with href "#region-of-origin-code-suffix" — so the quoted message and the "only rule DR1 enforces on this page" claim are both exact. Rubric 1 fired: I followed the journey past the page rather than stopping at the controller. CORRECT as a claim about the page; overstated as a claim about the journey, which the correction records.
finding.correction:
The claim stands and the slots are unchanged, but it is overstated in the way rubric 1 warns about, and whoever picks this up should know before they write the ticket. "The frontend lets them continue with nothing entered" is true of the page and false of the notification. obligations/sections/origin.js:27-36 declares regionOfOriginCode with an equalsGate on regionCodeRequirement: mandatory and in scope when the answer is 'yes', in scope and optional when it is 'no'. bridge/status/completeness/leaf.js and its index treat an in-scope, mandatory, unfulfilled leaf as unsatisfied, so with Yes selected and the code blank the origin task never reaches complete and the notification cannot be finished. The user is not silently let through — they are told late, at the hub, instead of at the point of the mistake, and they are not told which field is at fault. That is still real work and the difference slot describes the right fix; it is a missing inline error, not a missing rule. `medium` confidence is the right band given no error state was captured on either side.

The author also declined a mirror-image finding here — that DR1 validates only the region code and never requires a country of origin, where the frontend does — reading DR1's silence as a prototype limitation rather than an instruction to stop requiring the country. The verifier agrees, and the proof is firmer than the author had it. DR1's own completeness function hasOriginDetails at app/routes.js:231-244 returns false when countryOfOrigin is blank, and that function gates three things: the hub row's Complete status (:5756), the review card's error state (:4753) and hasReviewNotificationComplete (:4530). DR1 therefore treats the country of origin as mandatory and simply omits the inline error; it is the same defect as the one this finding reports, pointing the other way. Declining it was right and it should not be raised on a later pass.

relatedTo.why: both change the same revealed field, so they are cheapest done in one pass
